subject: Social Science
central_question: How do transport, communication, trade and tourism connect India and sustain its national economy?
in_scope_units: Transport, communication and trade as complementary lifelines of development.
Roadways and the classification and advantages of roads.
Railways, their distribution, importance and operational challenges.
Pipelines as specialised transport for liquids, gases and slurry.
Waterways, national waterways and major sea ports.
Personal and mass communication, postal, telecom and digital networks.
International trade, balance of trade and tourism as a trade activity.
banned_topics: Detailed industrial location from Manufacturing Industries.
Detailed mineral-pipeline production geography from Minerals and Energy Resources.
Detailed tourism case studies not stated in the chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Transport and communication are independent sectors.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes transport, communication and trade as complementary systems that together connect supply, demand and markets.

known_pitfalls.claim: Road transport is always cheaper than rail transport.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter gives road advantages mainly for short distances, smaller loads, difficult terrain, door-to-door service and feeder links.
They carry crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas, and solids can be transported when converted into slurry.

known_pitfalls.claim: A favourable balance of trade means imports are greater than exports.
known_pitfalls.correction: A favourable balance occurs when the value of exports exceeds the value of imports.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 2(i) to state three merits of roadways.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(ii) to explain where rail transport is most convenient.
Use NCERT Exercise 1(ii) to identify pipelines as reducing trans-shipment losses and delays.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(i) to explain why transport and communication are national lifelines.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(iv) to distinguish local and international trade.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with “EXERCISES”, Questions 1 to 3, followed by a quiz drive and a transport word-search activity.
